notes: Read the whole target, context and all ten candidates. Anchor present-relative assessments to 2008, neutralize rhetoric, resolve the sustainable-energy-policy and employment referents and retain the uncertainty about where jobs will be created instead of treating a question as a prediction. Preserve source assessments as such; retain original hearing, employment and procurement subclaims.

claims.claim_text: Participants in the Democratic Party's 2008 local platform hearings called for a sustainable U.S. energy policy addressing economic, national-security and environmental challenges.
The United States has historically taken action in response to new national-security threats or competitive conditions undermining U.S. economic leadership.
The Democratic Party's 2008 platform assesses the U.S. energy threat as possibly less immediate than threats from dictators but equally real and dangerous.
The Democratic Party's 2008 platform assesses opportunities from a sustainable-energy transition as greater than the dangers of the U.S. energy threat.
The Democratic Party's 2008 platform leaves open whether jobs developing new energy solutions will be created in the United States or abroad.
By the Democratic Party's 2008 platform, countries including Germany, Spain and Brazil had experienced economic growth from clean energy.
The Democratic Party's 2008 platform characterizes the United States as decades behind other countries in developing clean energy.
